title: Succinct Arguments for QMA in the Quantum Random Oracle Model
abstract: Succinct arguments are a fundamental cryptographic primitive for verifying computational claims with small communication. In the classical setting, succinct arguments for NP can be constructed from unstructured hardness alone (e.g., hash functions) by compiling probabilistically checkable proofs (PCPs) or interactive oracle proofs (IOPs) for NP via the commit-and-open paradigm. In contrast, known succinct arguments for QMA rely on ``structured'' cryptographic primitives, or on the quantum PCP conjecture.   We construct the first succinct argument for QMA in the quantum random oracle model (QROM) without relying on additional cryptographic assumptions or unproven conjectures. This yields succinct arguments for QMA from unstructured hardness alone, showing that ideal hash functions not only suffice for succinct arguments for NP but also for QMA.   Underlying our result is an efficiency-preserving transformation that compiles quantum interactive oracle proofs (QIOPs), a recently introduced interactive generalization of quantum PCPs, into quantum arguments for the same language, via a natural quantum commit-and-open paradigm. Our transformation applies to every QIOP with public-query soundness, a notion that we formalize to capture a natural requirement of the commit-and-open paradigm and is satisfied by a known QIOP for QMA. As a key ingredient in our transformation, we formalize and construct extractable vector commitments for quantum states with local openings in the QROM, which may be of independent interest.
summary: This paper achieves a major theoretical breakthrough by constructing the first succinct argument for QMA in the Quantum Random Oracle Model (QROM) using only unstructured hardness. It extends the classical commit-and-open paradigm to the quantum setting via a novel transformation of Quantum Interactive Oracle Proofs. This result significantly advances the understanding of verifiable quantum computation complexity.
main_problem: The core problem is constructing succinct arguments for QMA (Quantum Merlin-Arthur) in the Quantum Random Oracle Model (QROM) without relying on unproven conjectures or structured hardness assumptions.
main_result: The authors construct the first such succinct argument for QMA in the QROM, demonstrating that unstructured hardness alone suffices for this purpose.
method: The method involves a general, efficiency-preserving transformation that compiles Quantum Interactive Oracle Proofs (QIOPs) into quantum arguments (QARGs) using a quantum analogue of the classical commit-and-open paradigm.
model_or_system: The theoretical setting is the Quantum Random Oracle Model (QROM). The proof framework involves compiling QIOPs, which are interactive generalizations of quantum PCPs, into arguments.
key_observables: Communication complexity, soundness error, and the probability difference between simulation and extraction worlds.
important_parameters: The complexity is shown to be poly(lambda, log nu), where lambda and nu are related to the security parameters.
main_assumptions: The result relies on the QROM and the construction of extractable vector commitments for quantum states with local openings.
paper_structure: The paper develops the necessary quantum commitment schemes (QSVC) first, followed by the transformation that compiles QIOPs into QARGs, and finally, the analysis bounding the probability difference between simulation and extraction worlds.
why_interesting: While highly theoretical, the development of robust, unconditionally secure quantum cryptographic primitives like these commitments and arguments is foundational for any advanced quantum information theory work.
